identity_unit: exact House legislative action and governed source version

actions.mechanism:
Roll 278 is the July 22, 2026 final-passage vote on H.R. 8800, the FY 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, as amended by the House. It is one whole-package choice on a broad defense authorization bill with medical-care, military-family support, housing and veterans-health mechanisms. It is not a separate vote for or against every clinical service or benefit in that package. The exact floor proceeding reports the Committee amendments, agrees to them en gros, orders third reading, rejects bare recommittal 277 and then passes the bill 216–212, with 3 Not Voting. Passage is not enactment or actual implementation.

The voted floor base is RCP 119-33 under H.Res. 1438, together with adopted amendments. Material care, allowance, childcare, tenant and authorization clauses were checked against that base; adopted Part A 19, 29 and 31 supply material later changes. The later EH record supplies reviewed operative passages, not an assertion that its entire 2.98 million-character assembled package was independently reviewed. H.Res. 1438 section 11 directs inclusion at engrossment of separately House-passed S. 1383: later EH Division E/SAVE America Act is not a newly inferred component choice in roll 278. Failed Ukraine-funding amendment 264 and EO 14183-codification amendment 266 remain distinct failed choices, rather than operative passage components.

The Health mechanisms include no-premium/no-charge covered dental benefits for specified junior selected-reserve members and qualified space/resource-dependent dental access for dependents. Section 703 requires TRICARE Prime/Select fertility-care benefits for specified active-duty members and their dependents; former members are excluded. Its IVF terms include up to 3 oocyte retrievals per calendar year, single-embryo transfer unless medically indicated, ordinary benefit cost sharing and specified exclusions for uses of Defense funds. The fertility provision applies October 1, 2028; it is not immediate universal infertility coverage. Section 706 provides up to 365 days of uniform-formulary contraception for defined eligible active-duty members/dependents, at beneficiary option through named pharmacy channels. Its printed timing is beginning not less than 180 days after enactment, not a promise of coverage by day 180.

Section 705 prohibits identified March 4, 2026 service changes at 41 listed military treatment facilities and requires reversal/restoration within 30 days to the March 3 level, except a later law modifies that level. The listed changes include inpatient-to-outpatient conversion, limiting beneficiary access, and ending specified clinical services/contracts. The text does not itself prove those changes occurred or patients lost care. Other reviewed clauses address maternity-transfer continuity, care-scope administration, conditional health-financing accounts, sensitive-exam chaperones, transition notices, physical-therapy referral waivers, maternity/nurse staffing and complaints. The OB-exam present-chaperone requirement and the general offer-of-an-available-chaperone provision are distinct. Notices do not automatically extend eligibility; staffing contracts and reports do not establish actual access or clinical outcomes.

Adopted Part A 19 appears as section 709. It prohibits coverage or furnishing of the listed purpose-defined surgical procedures and pharmaceutical interventions, including specified non-genital procedures, when provided for the defined gender-related purpose; the printed first two disorder-of-sex-development exceptions refer to such minor, while the opening covered-member/dependent wording is not itself a universal under-18 qualifier. Separate 1077(b)(4)/1079(a)(20) changes remove the could-result-in-sterilization qualifier from the existing under-18 restriction. The dated 1076 eligibility/cross-reference and no-new-entitlement boundaries remain. This is not a ban on all uses of the listed drugs or a separate roll 278 choice endorsing that restriction; the previously interpreted amendment 267 has its own member observations.

Family-support provisions include qualified domestic-violence victim housing for up to one year; nonmedical military-family counseling through December 22, 2029; optional infant/toddler-capacity grants capped at 75 percent of expansion cost, with at least half of new capacity reserved for military children for 10 years and no displacement of enrolled nonmilitary children. In-home childcare provisions include participating State Department au pairs, specified State/local additional-condition preemption, direct payments to members or provider payments with written consent, and an existing-agreement exception to the 180 day implementation rule. Printed overlapping section 589 renumberings are not silently repaired. Section 611 excludes the member's full basic housing allowance from basic-needs gross household income rather than the dated discretionary partial exclusion. Other basic-needs conditions, including 200 percent FPL, active service, training, dependents and household/application rules, are not replaced by universal eligibility or a new income threshold. The dated statute's December 31, 2027 termination is not silently extended by 611. Additional reviewed support includes conditional CONUS cost-of-living payments, capped breast-milk shipping, naval meals, pregnancy-loss leave and qualified survivor benefits.

Housing provisions extend anti-reprisal reporting protection to named housing officials, inspectors general and Members of Congress, with modified notice/final-action responsibilities. Section 2813 prohibits a landlord from requesting an NDA from a tenant, former tenant or prospective tenant for leases or housing services; it replaces the dated 2890(f)(2)/(3) settlement/counsel and 10 business-day clauses with all-unit coverage and a tenant definition. It is broader than the older prohibition on requiring signatures and is not merely preservation of those deleted exceptions. Other reviewed clauses address work-order standards, habitability plans, safety notices and construction/design authorization using separately appropriated funds. No new home, repair or expenditure is asserted as accomplished.

Section 1405 authorizes FY 2027 Defense Health Program appropriations for eligible beneficiaries under the funding table; authorization is not an actual appropriation or a measured increase in total care spending. The joint Lovell Medical Center authority extends to September 30, 2028 and permits qualified transfer of 174 million dollars of authorized and available Defense Health Program operation/maintenance funds. Its printed use-of-funds cross-reference is retained without silently repairing subsection (a) to (b).

Adopted Part A 29 adds 1751–1753: a VA senior official for emerging therapeutic interventions, interagency coordination, research/activity reports, a workforce-readiness/training plan and a report on implementation of EO 14401. It does not itself make every psychedelic-assisted therapy approved treatment or prove safety/effectiveness. The printed report cadence is biannually; the candidate does not resolve that wording into an invented precise cadence or independently codify every provision of the referenced order. No separate individual member 29 vote is inferred from en bloc adoption.

Adopted Part A 31, reflected in 1726, says notwithstanding any other law that any pilot program authorized under this Act terminates at the earlier of two years after enactment or its own earlier date. That general rule qualifies longer nominal terms in medical/family pilot clauses. The candidate does not promise five or nine years of delivery from those printed terms, silently decide every existing-program extension or post-termination grant/contract obligation, or extend the rule to every non-pilot research activity.

Yea supports passage of this amended package; Nay opposes passage. These choices do not determine why a member voted, establish opposition/support for each separate benefit or restriction, resolve clinical outcomes, or erase different earlier amendment choices. The reviewed medical/family/housing/veterans mechanisms establish bounded Health membership; exhaustive package and episode completeness, all cross-references, implementation and external semantic acceptance remain unproven.

The original 8,349-character Health candidate above, its 23 claim bindings, all 26 governed witnesses, exact-action identity, meaning reference and limitations are preserved as the earlier bounded interpretation. The following prospective qualification follows actual reading of all 2,978,639 characters of the retained public EH text, selected native floor pages, the rule and material dated witnesses. Whole-text reading does not establish enactment, current law, every legal application, table arithmetic, a classified-annex or visual review, or independent editorial acceptance. The whole final-passage action remains the question; neither clinical excerpts nor a title or nationality keyword substitutes for the rest of the package.

The preserved Health paragraph's grouped1077/1079 wording is superseded for this qualified candidate by this exact prospective clarification: adopted§709 adds a new exclusion to1077(b) and separately deletes the could-result-in-sterilization qualifier from1079(a)(20). It does not delete a universal under-18 limit from both provisions. The purpose-defined treatment scope, exceptions printed with such minor, existing eligibility and no-new-entitlement rule remain; their legal interaction is not silently resolved. Earlier Health wording and its historical witness contract remain visible rather than overwritten.

H.Res.1438 deems RCP119-33 adopted as the floor base, permits the specified Part A amendments and en bloc procedure, and provides for engrossment and one motion to recommit. The July21 native Clerk designation includes Strong Part A10 in en bloc No.1; that package was agreed to. The broader Roy Part A2, offered by Boebert, would instead have replaced §521 with an all-foreign-country academy instruction prohibition. It was postponed after a voice-no outcome and rejected at recorded roll256,61–360 with15NotVoting. It is not an adopted component of passage278. Hinson's Part A34 was agreed to on July22; the Kelly Part A313 maritime title was included in en bloc No.5 and agreed to. Native July22 pages130/131 distinguish the failed bare recommittal277 from the subsequent voice question, Smith demand, ordered recorded passage278,216–212/3NotVoting. Later engrossment assembly under rule§11 adds the separately House-passed S.1383 text as DivisionE; this does not create another SAVE America component choice in roll278. The EH organization sentence still says four divisions while listing five. Printed disagreement in a debate speaker's en bloc label does not replace the formal Clerk designation.

The concrete48US1806 admission-date amendment below is distinct from military-school attendance, military-service qualifications or the mere possibility that immigrants benefit from medical care. Academy admission is not INA admission; foreign location alone does not convert military assistance into a refugee, parole, visa or removal rule. The previously interpreted academy amendment256, Ukraine-funding264, military-service EO266 and medical-treatment267 remain distinct earlier choices with their existing source-bound dispositions. Their observations and meanings are not replaced by this later whole-passage choice.

The accession amendment appears as §519A. It would add a 10US504(d) prohibition on enlistment of a person who is a national of a covered nation, notwithstanding §504(b), and would add a §532(a) original-appointment requirement that the person has not been a national of a covered nation during the preceding five years. These amendments apply to original enlistments or original appointments on or after180days after enactment. The one-year Secretary of Defense report concerns members who BOTH are foreign nationals of a covered nation AND were lawful permanent residents at accession, with accession dates, service years and numbers seeking citizenship. It does not order their discharge or revoke citizenship. The retained2024§504(b) already distinguishes US nationals, lawful permanent residents, Compact categories and a conditional critical-skill enlistment authority. Retained§532 separately requires citizenship and other qualifications and permits only its specified citizenship waiver for lawful permanent residents or specified US nationals, below major/lieutenant commander, when national security requires. The new text is not a general repeal of those qualifications or a statement that every foreign-born person is ineligible. Its printed §4872(f) references and the same package's §1803 replacement of that section require the cross-reference qualification below; no unambiguous individual eligibility determination is asserted.

Section521 would add a prohibition on instruction at or attendance at a service academy under10US347 by a foreign national of a covered nation, using its printed §4872 definition reference. It is narrower than the rejected all-foreign-country replacement. The retained2024§347 otherwise authorizes selected foreign attendance, up to80 at each academy, plus separately bounded exchanges and short cultural activities. Its reimbursement rule includes a Secretary of Defense whole-or-part waiver; graduation does not itself confer entitlement to a US military appointment. Floor debate references to60 students or invariably full reimbursement are attributed statements, not substitutes for that dated statute. This candidate does not infer that the passage vote supported or opposed a particular foreign student, admission or commission.

Section529 requires the Secretary of Defense to establish by January1,2028 a foreign-student SeniorROTC participation program using existing10US2103(b), with a September30,2027 strategy, reporting and a December31,2032 termination. Existing2103(b) permits foreign enrollment when the relevant military Secretary approves under criteria approved by the Secretary of State. Section529 denies use of its authority for participating foreign students' tuition or room and board; it does not issue visas, guarantee selection or create a commission entitlement. Separate§605 removes the first-year-course condition from10US2103a(a), not from2103(a). The dated2103a(b) citizenship, enlistment and loyalty requirements are not deleted by that operand. Its contracting-bonus changes do not waive all military or immigration eligibility conditions.

Section1705 changes only the date in48US1806(b)(1)(B), before December31,2029 to before December31,2035. The retained2024 provision concerns otherwise-qualified H-2B workers, up to three years notwithstanding the temporary-service requirement, for specified military-realignment-related contractor work OR specified healthcare work at joint-serving facilities on Guam or the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. The healthcare branch retains applicable education, training and licensing conditions and excludes medical-school graduates coming to practice medicine. The location limitation and otherwise-qualified language remain. The retained law's separate transition endpoint and the §1806(b)(1)(A) transition linkage are not changed by the printed1705 operand; their interaction and any intervening law remain application questions. This is not a blanket extension of every CNMI transition/CW-1 rule, a waiver of all admission or labor requirements, or guaranteed admission through2035. EnactedDecember2025§1703 is a different, already enacted Wake Island authority with its own otherwise-qualified seeking, cap, cancellation, transfer and time-window conditions; it is not silently restated as the July1705 amendment.

Adopted Part A34 appears as §3118. It prohibits obligation or expenditure of funds authorized by this Act or otherwise available for FY2027 for DOE for a defined National Laboratory that authorizes a covered visitor's admission to a nonpublic area. A covered visitor is a foreign national from a country of concern under enactedPL119-60§8512 who is NOT a DOE employee or the laboratory's management-and-operations contractor employee AND has requested access to the laboratory's premises, information or technology; lawful permanent residents are excluded. The incorporated8512 definition is the People's Republic of China, including Hong Kong and Macau. It is not the four-country §4872 list, every foreign scientist or birthplace/ethnicity. The laboratory term retains its42US15801 statutory definition. Broader country lists or direct visitor-ban shorthand in debate do not replace this funding prohibition and its conjunctive predicates.

Section1803 prints an entire replacement of10US4872. Its covered-nation definition is in proposed(m)(5) and lists North Korea, China, Russia and Iran. Proposed(m)(13) United States person includes a US citizen, a lawful permanent resident, OR a domestically organized entity whose ultimate beneficial ownership AND control are with those persons; it is not citizenship alone. The replacement has distinct sourcing restrictions and exceptions. Proposed4872(g) gives the Secretary of Defense one conditional authority to waive(d) or(e), in whole or part, for a procurement, covered item, Tier1 or Tier2 material or supply-chain stage, including a combination or class. The waiver must be written and identify with specificity the covered materials/circumstances AND its period AND factual basis; determine insufficient Tier1 production by domestically owned entities or insufficient Tier2 production outside covered nations, in quantity, quality or form to meet timely defense needs on reasonable terms; determine that absence of the waiver would significantly adversely affect NATIONAL SECURITY OR defense production OR readiness OR sustainment OR timely contract performance; AND provide a transition plan. The adverse-effect determination may be based on or informed by a4863(k) national-security waiver, but that does not replace the other(g)(1) prerequisites. The transition plan includes quantifiable mitigation milestones/timelines, a requirement that the contractor enter binding supplier agreements before expiry that will result in compliance and obviate a future waiver/renewal, and any contractual considerations the Secretary determines appropriate. An upstream-material waiver does not cover downstream forms unless it expressly says so. A waiver may last up to two years and may be renewed without a numerical limit only on a new written determination satisfying paragraph(1). It cannot take effect until congressional-defense-committee notice and30days, or certified urgent need and7days; notice includes specificity, period, factual basis and principal mitigation measures. Contractors must supply reasonably available supporting documentation as prescribed. These are conjunctive sourcing-waiver conditions, not separate general national-security and nonavailability waiver paths. The general180day applicability rule and special Tier2 timing remain distinct, and none establishes a personal immigration ban. Elsewhere the package still prints references to4872(f),4872(d) and older subparagraphs. The retained2024 law and selected enacted2025 amendments are dated witnesses, not permission to silently repair those references or certify the outcome of all overlapping amendments. Proposed nationality/control definitions, effective dates, constitutional and individual applications remain qualified by these printed legal questions.

For the remotely crewed offshore supply-vessel pilot in§3555, all operating functions, including navigation, engineering and monitoring, must be performed by credentialed US citizens, with the same crew complement size and certification currently required for that vessel type, size and power. Eligibility is limited to specified coastwise-qualified12112 vessels built OR repaired in US shipyards within five years, no more than6,000deadweight tons/350feet, operating remotely in the Gulf beyond12nautical miles. The Commandant's design/crew-accommodation regulation modifications or waivers remain subject to navigation and safe/secure-operation conditions; they do not waive the printed operating-personnel citizenship requirement. Retained12112 has its own documentation and build/prize/forfeiture/wreck/other-law conditions. Although3555 prints a five-year nominal pilot term,1726's notwithstanding-law earlier-of-two-years-or-own-earlier-date rule must be retained; no five-year delivery promise or universal pilot-extension/post-termination conclusion follows.

Sections3563,3564 and3566 print different maritime education, credential-cost reimbursement and training-cruise assistance mechanisms. They respectively use proposed51512,51708 and51513 and expressly condition the relevant individual assistance on US citizenship. The Secretary MAY make the described agreements/payments; academy, credential, transportation-worker credential, medical, service, reporting, funding and nonduplication conditions remain. In3563/3566, the waiver or alternative-service provisions are limited to terms in subsection(c), rather than an authority to waive the subsection(a) citizenship condition. The3564 reimbursement branch requires the specified sea service OR qualifying shoreside work and retains the$10,000-per-year and other-source/program exclusions; its printed10,0000gross-register-ton wording is not repaired. These are not universal benefits or new personal entry/employment rights.

The separately printed3687 proposed51512 concerns academy fuel and crew funding, and3688 proposed51513 concerns predominantly private sea-term scholarships and student agreements. They are not silently merged with the3563/3566 texts merely because proposed Code numbers overlap; their actors, funds, service and eligibility wording differ. Section3688 does not print the same express citizenship clause as3566, but that observation does not establish that any particular noncitizen qualifies under all credential/academy/other laws. Section3683 directs a maritime exchange program limited to US citizens and citizens of NATO members, US treaty allies and major non-NATO allies, and directs the Maritime Administrator to seek corporate/government placement partners. It does not itself issue visas or guarantee a placement.

Section3691 adds periodic, at-least-annual inspection of defined offshore facilities to verify a valid43US1356(c) exemption, and confirmation that crew ALREADY REQUIRED to hold a TWIC under70105 have one. The dated1356(a)(3) regulation concerns US citizens OR lawful permanent residents and retains(c)'s contractual/registry, worker-availability, national-interest and foreign-ownership/control/reciprocity exceptions. Dated70105 has defined access/credential categories, security and immigration checks, waiver/appeal and privacy rules; it is not a universal citizens-only crew rule. The July inspection language does not itself repeal those exceptions or impose a TWIC on every person aboard every vessel.

Section3569's proposed vessel-preference subchapter concerns defined inbound containerized and roll-on/roll-off vehicle cargo within designated trade lanes, with entity/group participation targets, mariner/fleet/capacity findings and specified phase adjustments. It expressly disclaims a uniform nationwide cargo quota. Its qualification condition distinguishes a vessel owned, chartered, managed or operated by or for an entity subject to foreign ownership, control or influence from an entity determined not to be so subject; the former needs an approved M-SSA. The separate country-of-concern prohibition combines a citizen's country status with a direct or indirect controlling interest OR other disqualifying influence in the owner/charterer/manager/operator. Nationality alone is not the complete printed predicate.

For the M-SSA framework, the Secretary of Transportation must establish regulations in consultation with Defense and Homeland Security, while the Maritime Administrator MAY approve an agreement only with the three printed certification/compliance/consultation conditions. The covered entity must maintain the specified US-citizen executive, citizen governance and operational-control arrangements, citizen-only security committee, citizen compliance officers and sensitive-information firewalls. These are specified operational/governance roles, not a rule that every foreign investor or employee is prohibited. The agreement's entity/vessel scope, change notice/approval, audit, breach/remedy and information-security conditions remain. Its limited deeming concerns an approved entity being United States-controlled, with the separate capital-origin condition; it does not naturalize anyone or confer coastwise privileges. Existing documentation, safety, security, labor and other national-security reviews are not waived. Printed references to regulations under55353(j), the55352 content/deeming cross-references, duplicate definition number6, overlapping2042 threshold, and PhaseI's minimum four-year pilot-period language alongside1726 remain application questions, without silently selecting a repaired provision or imposing a two-year end on the whole cargo regime.

The country definitions are not interchangeable. Section3569 imports countries identified under15US4651(7). That dated definition enumerates category(A), a covered nation under its printed4872(d) reference, and category(B), any country the Commerce Secretary determines, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, Secretary of State and Director of National Intelligence, engages in conduct detrimental to US national security or foreign policy. Section3604 separately enumerates a covered-nation category(A) under its own printed4872(d) reference and category(B), any country the Maritime Administrator so determines in consultation with the named Defense/State/Intelligence officials AND the Chair of the Federal Maritime Commission. The literal connecting and is retained as an enumeration of the two described country categories, not a requirement that a country satisfy both category descriptions. The Commerce and Maritime actors/consultations and printed outdated or overlapping references remain distinct and qualified. Neither definition is silently replaced with3118's China/HongKong/Macau definition or a universal fixed-country list. Section3569's incorporated-reference and application questions are not resolved by restating the enumeration.

Section3604's foreign-entity definition separately describes foreign government/party, natural-person and foreign-organization branches and broader owned/controlled/directed, agent/employee, substantial-equity, managerial and country-citizenship/residence inclusion branches. The natural-person branch excludes lawful permanent residents, US citizens and other protected individuals under8US1324b(a)(3). The dated protected-individual definition includes US nationals and specified temporary residents, refugees and asylees with its printed qualifications. The independent express LPR exclusion is not removed merely by a qualification in the other-protected-person branch. Conversely, that one natural-person branch does not erase the other agency/control/inclusion limbs. No individual is classified by birthplace or ethnicity. This title's distinct foreign-entity-of-concern alternatives include particular designations, lists, jurisdiction/control, alleged activity with obtained convictions, carrier findings and a specified official determination; it does not label every foreign national a terrorist, sanctioned person or immigration offender.

Sections1041–1043 change the named2019 Guantanamo funding restrictions' December31,2026 endpoints to December31,2027;1044 changes the named2018 station-control restriction's fiscal-year endpoint2026 to2027. The selected original1033 restriction concerns its named/qualified detainee population and transfer/release assistance to or within the United States, territories or possessions, not all migrants. Original1034 includes its Guantanamo-facility modification exception and the incorporated2015 defined population; original1035 names Libya, Somalia, Syria and Yemen. The station provision concerns closing/abandoning, relinquishing control to Cuba or the specified constructive treaty change. The selected enacted2025 extensions supply the2026 operands. These dated original and intervening witnesses do not establish exhaustive current law or permit importing an unrestricted detention/transfer rule. Section1045 separately inserts an exclusion for a US citizen into FY2012§1021(b)'s covered-person definition under the named AUMF framework. The retained1021/1022 text has specific hostile-conduct/person predicates and savings/other-law rules. Excluding citizens from that definition is not a new authority to detain every noncitizen or a resolution of constitutional or individual detention questions.

Section1081(jj) strikes FY2022NDAA§1324. The complete original1324 requires recurring notices of OAW or successor-operation transportation, housing, medical and other sustainment costs for Afghan special-immigrant-visa applicants and other Afghans at risk, and whether those funds were reimbursable. Repealing that notification is not itself repeal of all OAW spending, assistance or admission authorities. The bill's label and the baseline's civic-aid wording remain separate literal texts. Section1082 extends the named quarterly southwest-border support briefing endpoint from2026 to2027, retaining the original briefing's planning, personnel-risk, Mexico-cooperation, support, readiness and recommendation subjects; it does not direct a new deployment or confer an admission or arrest power.

The actual border common-picture provision is1089R, which requires a Secretary of Defense plan within180days and later communication to interagency partners the Secretary considers appropriate. Its architecture/data sources, sharing procedures and authorities, cybersecurity/data protection, coordination with named domestic and authorized international partners, phased schedule, resources, training and effectiveness metrics are plan requirements, not proof of deployed capability or unrestricted surveillance. Separate1089 concerns autonomous-warfare doctrine and is not substituted for1089R. Section1099A directs a named operation for specified southwest-border support and the related budget/request/oversight reporting, and expressly disclaims authorization of military force. Its definition includes specified planning/logistics/intelligence/aviation/engineering support but expressly excludes support provided to a civilian law-enforcement agency; that printed tension is retained. Section1065 calls for a revised instrument named Department of Defense Instruction3025.18 requiring reassessment of immediate-response necessity no later than one week after the request, plus notification of issuance by the printed deadline. It does not authorize limitless response. The Instruction label in1065 and Directive label in1099A, incorporated versions and any resulting legal application are not silently repaired or certified.

Section416 strikes32US112(e), whose dated text limits specified year-end Guard counterdrug staffing to4,000 with a conditional up-to20percent national-security increase. The remaining State-plan, non-Federal-service, law-authorization, training/readiness and other limitations are not all repealed by that operand. Section1095 raises the112(a)(3) equipment amount from$15,000 to$25,000 per item; the dated clause's advance Secretary approval for equipment above the amount remains, rather than an absolute no-exception ceiling or an appropriation. Section1094 changes10US284(i)(3)'s small-scale-construction definition from$1million to$2million per project and adds minor military construction to the existing notification-description clause. The operative definition amendment is not restricted solely by its foreign-partner heading. Neither amount change supplies a general immigration arrest/deployment authority. The416 redesignation/report-reference questions are retained against the dated source without claiming all intervening codification is resolved.

Section1730 requires expanded interagency fentanyl/precursor coordination, including joint operations with HHS and the Attorney General, and a gaps report; it does not itself create an unbounded new arrest power. Section1733 requires recurring engagement/assessment of counter-tunnel technologies with DHS, including the Border Patrol subterranean office, and reports/briefings on opportunities and barriers; it is not proof of actual technology deployment. Section1738's report concerns an organization engaged in narcotics production/trafficking AND meeting at least one of its specified FTO, named sanctions-order or FEND-organized-crime predicates, through the printed2030 endpoint. Migrant nationality or border crossing alone does not meet that definition. Section1116 restricts use of FY2027DoD funds to implement a hiring freeze on specified categories, including positions essential to immigration enforcement, national security or public safety. It does not itself hire a particular number of personnel or turn every DoD position into an immigration-enforcement job.

Section1099L requires suspension or revocation of clearance or classified-access eligibility for a retired or separated Armed Forces member or a DoD civilian employee for lobbying activity/contact on behalf of an entity on BOTH the1260H Chinese-military-company report and the Treasury Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex list. The Secretary MAY waive for up to180days per period upon a certification that doing so is in the NATIONAL SECURITY INTEREST of the United States. This is not an all-foreign-employment prohibition or a generic national-interest waiver; its printed lobbying-definition exception reference remains a legal question. In distinct1741, the financial-app/device restriction has organizational or control branches. The natural-person control branch combines PRC nationality AND residence in the PRC AND beneficial ownership of MORE THAN25percent of voting securities; nationality alone is not sufficient. The official-capacity law-enforcement, intelligence, national-security, cybersecurity and enforcement/supervisory exception also requires the named Secretary/designee authorization. Neither provision changes citizenship or issues a visa.

Section227 creates a defense biotechnology prize program and expressly imports15US3719(g)(3): a private entity must be incorporated in AND maintain a primary place of business in the United States, while an individual, singly or in a group, must be a citizen OR permanent resident. The imported condition is not citizens-only and does not require every employee of an eligible entity to be a US citizen. Private-sector judging under the referenced3719(k) is separately subject to the printed conflict and fairness rules; the prize eligibility sentence is not a visa or commissioning entitlement. Other legal, funding, licensing and implementation limits are not waived by this description.

Section1102's Secretary of Defense MAY education-waiver authority has a competency/pathway determination, a five-year expiry, express statutory/licensure/professional and specified OPM scientific/technical exceptions, and an18month job-announcement applicability rule. It is not a waiver of every citizenship, immigration, security or appointment requirement. Separate1104 expands4093(b)(1)(B)'s eligible educational pathways and changes the connector in the named external-service agreement findings from AND to OR: in the dated4093(c)(1)(B)(ii), the nonemployee's external placement requires the Secretary to be unable to find an appropriate DoD position OR determine that the external employment benefits DoD. Written service obligations and other criteria remain. The dated4093(b)(1)(A) US-citizen/qualified TTCP-country branch and(g)'s limit on new foreign participants are not deleted by those operands. The1103 intern provision uses an institution definition from HEA102, a student-in-good-standing and Secretary qualification/background-check determination, voluntary supervised duties and limits, rather than conferring a visa or guaranteed future job.

For direct hiring,1110 preserves5US3303,3307 and3328 while authorizing qualified instructor-pilot/simulator appointments, and1122 preserves3303 and3328 for its specified industrial/range/test positions, with an advanced-degree requirement in its named scientific/engineering branch. Their without-regard language has a specified Title5 subchapter scope; it is not a waiver of all law or all nationality/security conditions. The separately proposed1599k texts in1102 and1122,1110's incomplete incentive citation, and the printed repeals/codification references remain unresolved legal questions. Section653 adds an express direction to apply37US908 in the same extent and manner to foreign-government employment/compensation, payments or awards obtained indirectly through a private entity by a retired Army/Navy/Marine/AirForce/SpaceForce member, or a Reserve member of those forces not on an active-duty call/order exceeding30days, under the relevant military Secretary. The dated908 has distinct employment/compensation Secretary-AND-State approval and not-contrary-to-national-interests findings, versus its other payment/award approval branch. This does not establish a general ban on every foreign employer, extend the new indirect clause to every uniformed-service population, or certify the novelty of all current indirect-employment law.

Section1075 requires military-college disclosure of gifts or covered contracts from the defined foreign source at the printed$50,000 annual-source aggregation threshold, with separate30day restricted/conditional-gift reports and the named regular-report dates, public reporting and enforcement. Its natural-person foreign-source branch refers to an individual who is neither a US citizen nor US national; other government/entity/agent branches remain. It does not equate every noncitizen with a foreign source, prohibit all gifts or create a new admission category. The donor-citizenship/residence and entity-incorporation/business-location attribution rules are reporting rules, not individual immigration determinations.

Section1526's contract/MOA condition, beginning270days after enactment, concerns IT made commercially available to customers in a country of concern OR providers with operations, subsidiaries or personnel located there. It is a location/business condition, not a test of every worker's nationality. The MOA requires DoD-first vulnerability disclosure before advance disclosure to another entity and no advance disclosure to a defined covered company. Its covered-company, control and country-reference conditions remain. The Secretary MAY waive case by case on written certification that the procurement action is required in the NATIONAL INTEREST, which is the actual1526 standard; it is not silently substituted with1099L's national-security standard. Printed4872(f) and overlapping amendment questions remain.

Section2844's connectivity pilot has a defined military-installation/population scope and multiple contract, equipment, security, availability and funding conditions. Its American-contracted-entity definition requires US organization AND principal place of business, the printed majority-ownership/control US-citizen-or-LPR or US-exchange/public-jurisdiction branch, and primarily US-BASED personnel for named functions. A location requirement is not a citizens-only staffing condition; the ownership and public-trading branches are not collapsed. Its supply-chain/source references and1726 interaction remain legal questions; no guaranteed five-year program, visa or entitlement for all civilians is inferred.

Sections353/354 separately address DoD freight-carrier certifications and a carrier registry. The certification is to the carrier's best knowledge after reasonable inquiry, covers ownership/control/significant-business relationships with the named listed companies, and flows down to its subcontractor/owner-operator contracting chain. The registry has operating/DoD qualifications, listed-or-designated-entity vetting, periodic revetting, a one-year contracting restriction and a Secretary of Defense exigency waiver. Drivers/personnel must meet security standards COMPARABLE TO TWIC OR other relevant Federal programs; that is not a newly printed rule that all drivers must be US citizens or physically hold a TWIC. The civil-penalty reference to18US1001 remains as printed, without substituting a repaired enforcement provision.

Section1413's traceability-provider requirements are conjunctive: US organization, ownership AND control by a United States person, and its separate printed foreign-ownership/control/influence condition. The incorporated26US7701(a)(30) definition includes a citizen OR resident, domestic partnerships/corporations and specified estates/trusts; it is not citizens-only and does not determine lawful immigration status. The provider remains a noncustodial traceability/verification service rather than a physical materials operator. Pilot phase/report timing,1726 and other contracting/security conditions remain; no automatic award or individual status benefit follows. Section1813 has a qualified domestic-company professional-services preference, documented nonapplication options and priority rules for existing procurement preferences. It retains organization AND principal-business criteria, its printed not-owned-and-controlled-by-a-foreign-entity condition, the DFARS definition reference and its at-least50percent qualifying-joint-venture branch. It is not an all-foreign-employee ban or a preference that always defeats other procurement law.

Section2825 concerns significant data-facility components manufactured in, or by an entity domiciled in or subject to the jurisdiction of, its listed countries, through enhanced-use-lease terms; it does not prohibit people merely because of their nationality. Section2829 requires a report and expresses a sense of Congress about property-related national-security risks and defined foreign-control relationships. It does not itself prohibit every foreign person's property purchase or enact a new general immigration prohibition. Section1214's DoD-assistance restriction has named Taliban/Afghan-government recipients and related entities, with an intent-to-forward predicate for the other entity/country branch. It is not an all-Afghan-person aid ban. Section1262 calls for a threat-network study/report, including trafficking or facilitating mass migration among its prioritization subjects; it does not define all migrants as criminals or authorize a general use of military force.

Sections1764/1765 provide US-citizenship and other stated qualifications for the nine UAP-records Review Board members and its executive director, with the director counted among the nine under the printed cross-reference. Nomination, conflicts, legacy-program involvement and security-clearance conditions remain. The staff text separately says citizen of integrity and impartiality with its printed exception/ethics consultation, and permits conditional employment before clearance while restricting protected-material access and requiring termination if necessary clearances are denied. The1744/1745/1764/1765 references are not silently repaired. These are the named records-review roles, not an amendment to all federal-job eligibility or factual proof of the phenomena the records concern.

Section513 would add a direction that, in carrying out50US3802(a), the Selective Service Director SHALL NOT register a person whose name appears in the defined Death Master File. It further amends the statute as amended by enactedFY2026§535 and says its change takes effect as if included in that earlier enactment. The selected enacted535 has its own one-year delayed effective date, registration population and exception; the dated2024 statute and that replacement are different versions. This is not an assertion that automatic registration was already operational at the July vote, a new induction or citizenship/status rule, or proof that every record is accurate. The printed2013/PublicLaw113-167/42US1306c definition reference and interaction of the timing clauses remain without silent repair.

Section514's military-personnel merit and race/ethnicity/national-origin provisions retain the limited unconventional-foreign-mission tasking exception, combatant-commander approval and report. They are not silently treated as a repeal of every separate citizenship or nationality qualification elsewhere in the package. Section1203's Inter-Pacific military education authority is discretionary, limited to the specified region/assistance-eligible countries and State concurrence, and preserves prohibitions under other law; associated transportation, supplies, billeting, health services or living allowances are not a general visa, admission or commission entitlement. Section1249's FAS-related analysis/plan/report concerns PRC influence in the named Freely Associated States; it does not amend their Compact entry rights. Its missing(c) reference and printed subsection numbering remain questions. Section2824 requires a visitor-processing capability at a domestic installation gate and direction to the appropriate office; it does not dispense with access screening or create immigration admission rights.

The whole package also contains procurement, defense research, military strength, foreign assistance, construction and funding-table provisions. Foreign manufacture, corporate control, tax residence, physical location, military-school attendance and nationality qualifications are not interchangeable concepts. The concrete H-2B admission-date operand and the bounded mechanisms above are not replaced by a keyword tally. Public tables were read as text; no visual/arithmetic audit, actual appropriation, individual outcome, exhaustive current-law/codification or classified-annex certificate is claimed. Printed overlapping proposed Code sections, regulatory references, timing, savings and constitutional/application questions remain available for independent review rather than silently resolved.

Yea supports passage of this whole exact amended package; Nay opposes passage. Neither determines a separate position on each national-status, border, medical, family, maritime, procurement or research component, a preferred alternative, motive, ideology, future behavior or the actual legal outcome for an individual. Present and Not Voting, if relevant to any other record, remain non-directional statuses. The current action is a source-qualified candidate pending independent semantic/domain review and editorial acceptance, without publication or production authorization.
actions.candidate_exact_action_meaning:
Roll 278 is the July 22, 2026 final-passage vote on H.R. 8800, the FY 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, as amended by the House. It is one whole-package choice on a broad defense authorization bill with medical-care, military-family support, housing and veterans-health mechanisms. It is not a separate vote for or against every clinical service or benefit in that package. The exact floor proceeding reports the Committee amendments, agrees to them en gros, orders third reading, rejects bare recommittal 277 and then passes the bill 216–212, with 3 Not Voting. Passage is not enactment or actual implementation.

The voted floor base is RCP 119-33 under H.Res. 1438, together with adopted amendments. Material care, allowance, childcare, tenant and authorization clauses were checked against that base; adopted Part A 19, 29 and 31 supply material later changes. The later EH record supplies reviewed operative passages, not an assertion that its entire 2.98 million-character assembled package was independently reviewed. H.Res. 1438 section 11 directs inclusion at engrossment of separately House-passed S. 1383: later EH Division E/SAVE America Act is not a newly inferred component choice in roll 278. Failed Ukraine-funding amendment 264 and EO 14183-codification amendment 266 remain distinct failed choices, rather than operative passage components.

The Health mechanisms include no-premium/no-charge covered dental benefits for specified junior selected-reserve members and qualified space/resource-dependent dental access for dependents. Section 703 requires TRICARE Prime/Select fertility-care benefits for specified active-duty members and their dependents; former members are excluded. Its IVF terms include up to 3 oocyte retrievals per calendar year, single-embryo transfer unless medically indicated, ordinary benefit cost sharing and specified exclusions for uses of Defense funds. The fertility provision applies October 1, 2028; it is not immediate universal infertility coverage. Section 706 provides up to 365 days of uniform-formulary contraception for defined eligible active-duty members/dependents, at beneficiary option through named pharmacy channels. Its printed timing is beginning not less than 180 days after enactment, not a promise of coverage by day 180.

Section 705 prohibits identified March 4, 2026 service changes at 41 listed military treatment facilities and requires reversal/restoration within 30 days to the March 3 level, except a later law modifies that level. The listed changes include inpatient-to-outpatient conversion, limiting beneficiary access, and ending specified clinical services/contracts. The text does not itself prove those changes occurred or patients lost care. Other reviewed clauses address maternity-transfer continuity, care-scope administration, conditional health-financing accounts, sensitive-exam chaperones, transition notices, physical-therapy referral waivers, maternity/nurse staffing and complaints. The OB-exam present-chaperone requirement and the general offer-of-an-available-chaperone provision are distinct. Notices do not automatically extend eligibility; staffing contracts and reports do not establish actual access or clinical outcomes.

Adopted Part A 19 appears as section 709. It prohibits coverage or furnishing of the listed purpose-defined surgical procedures and pharmaceutical interventions, including specified non-genital procedures, when provided for the defined gender-related purpose; the printed first two disorder-of-sex-development exceptions refer to such minor, while the opening covered-member/dependent wording is not itself a universal under-18 qualifier. Separate 1077(b)(4)/1079(a)(20) changes remove the could-result-in-sterilization qualifier from the existing under-18 restriction. The dated 1076 eligibility/cross-reference and no-new-entitlement boundaries remain. This is not a ban on all uses of the listed drugs or a separate roll 278 choice endorsing that restriction; the previously interpreted amendment 267 has its own member observations.

Family-support provisions include qualified domestic-violence victim housing for up to one year; nonmedical military-family counseling through December 22, 2029; optional infant/toddler-capacity grants capped at 75 percent of expansion cost, with at least half of new capacity reserved for military children for 10 years and no displacement of enrolled nonmilitary children. In-home childcare provisions include participating State Department au pairs, specified State/local additional-condition preemption, direct payments to members or provider payments with written consent, and an existing-agreement exception to the 180 day implementation rule. Printed overlapping section 589 renumberings are not silently repaired. Section 611 excludes the member's full basic housing allowance from basic-needs gross household income rather than the dated discretionary partial exclusion. Other basic-needs conditions, including 200 percent FPL, active service, training, dependents and household/application rules, are not replaced by universal eligibility or a new income threshold. The dated statute's December 31, 2027 termination is not silently extended by 611. Additional reviewed support includes conditional CONUS cost-of-living payments, capped breast-milk shipping, naval meals, pregnancy-loss leave and qualified survivor benefits.

Housing provisions extend anti-reprisal reporting protection to named housing officials, inspectors general and Members of Congress, with modified notice/final-action responsibilities. Section 2813 prohibits a landlord from requesting an NDA from a tenant, former tenant or prospective tenant for leases or housing services; it replaces the dated 2890(f)(2)/(3) settlement/counsel and 10 business-day clauses with all-unit coverage and a tenant definition. It is broader than the older prohibition on requiring signatures and is not merely preservation of those deleted exceptions. Other reviewed clauses address work-order standards, habitability plans, safety notices and construction/design authorization using separately appropriated funds. No new home, repair or expenditure is asserted as accomplished.

Section 1405 authorizes FY 2027 Defense Health Program appropriations for eligible beneficiaries under the funding table; authorization is not an actual appropriation or a measured increase in total care spending. The joint Lovell Medical Center authority extends to September 30, 2028 and permits qualified transfer of 174 million dollars of authorized and available Defense Health Program operation/maintenance funds. Its printed use-of-funds cross-reference is retained without silently repairing subsection (a) to (b).

Adopted Part A 29 adds 1751–1753: a VA senior official for emerging therapeutic interventions, interagency coordination, research/activity reports, a workforce-readiness/training plan and a report on implementation of EO 14401. It does not itself make every psychedelic-assisted therapy approved treatment or prove safety/effectiveness. The printed report cadence is biannually; the candidate does not resolve that wording into an invented precise cadence or independently codify every provision of the referenced order. No separate individual member 29 vote is inferred from en bloc adoption.

Adopted Part A 31, reflected in 1726, says notwithstanding any other law that any pilot program authorized under this Act terminates at the earlier of two years after enactment or its own earlier date. That general rule qualifies longer nominal terms in medical/family pilot clauses. The candidate does not promise five or nine years of delivery from those printed terms, silently decide every existing-program extension or post-termination grant/contract obligation, or extend the rule to every non-pilot research activity.

Yea supports passage of this amended package; Nay opposes passage. These choices do not determine why a member voted, establish opposition/support for each separate benefit or restriction, resolve clinical outcomes, or erase different earlier amendment choices. The reviewed medical/family/housing/veterans mechanisms establish bounded Health membership; exhaustive package and episode completeness, all cross-references, implementation and external semantic acceptance remain unproven.

The original 8,349-character Health candidate above, its 23 claim bindings, all 26 governed witnesses, exact-action identity, meaning reference and limitations are preserved as the earlier bounded interpretation. The following prospective qualification follows actual reading of all 2,978,639 characters of the retained public EH text, selected native floor pages, the rule and material dated witnesses. Whole-text reading does not establish enactment, current law, every legal application, table arithmetic, a classified-annex or visual review, or independent editorial acceptance. The whole final-passage action remains the question; neither clinical excerpts nor a title or nationality keyword substitutes for the rest of the package.

The preserved Health paragraph's grouped1077/1079 wording is superseded for this qualified candidate by this exact prospective clarification: adopted§709 adds a new exclusion to1077(b) and separately deletes the could-result-in-sterilization qualifier from1079(a)(20). It does not delete a universal under-18 limit from both provisions. The purpose-defined treatment scope, exceptions printed with such minor, existing eligibility and no-new-entitlement rule remain; their legal interaction is not silently resolved. Earlier Health wording and its historical witness contract remain visible rather than overwritten.

H.Res.1438 deems RCP119-33 adopted as the floor base, permits the specified Part A amendments and en bloc procedure, and provides for engrossment and one motion to recommit. The July21 native Clerk designation includes Strong Part A10 in en bloc No.1; that package was agreed to. The broader Roy Part A2, offered by Boebert, would instead have replaced §521 with an all-foreign-country academy instruction prohibition. It was postponed after a voice-no outcome and rejected at recorded roll256,61–360 with15NotVoting. It is not an adopted component of passage278. Hinson's Part A34 was agreed to on July22; the Kelly Part A313 maritime title was included in en bloc No.5 and agreed to. Native July22 pages130/131 distinguish the failed bare recommittal277 from the subsequent voice question, Smith demand, ordered recorded passage278,216–212/3NotVoting. Later engrossment assembly under rule§11 adds the separately House-passed S.1383 text as DivisionE; this does not create another SAVE America component choice in roll278. The EH organization sentence still says four divisions while listing five. Printed disagreement in a debate speaker's en bloc label does not replace the formal Clerk designation.

The concrete48US1806 admission-date amendment below is distinct from military-school attendance, military-service qualifications or the mere possibility that immigrants benefit from medical care. Academy admission is not INA admission; foreign location alone does not convert military assistance into a refugee, parole, visa or removal rule. The previously interpreted academy amendment256, Ukraine-funding264, military-service EO266 and medical-treatment267 remain distinct earlier choices with their existing source-bound dispositions. Their observations and meanings are not replaced by this later whole-passage choice.

The accession amendment appears as §519A. It would add a 10US504(d) prohibition on enlistment of a person who is a national of a covered nation, notwithstanding §504(b), and would add a §532(a) original-appointment requirement that the person has not been a national of a covered nation during the preceding five years. These amendments apply to original enlistments or original appointments on or after180days after enactment. The one-year Secretary of Defense report concerns members who BOTH are foreign nationals of a covered nation AND were lawful permanent residents at accession, with accession dates, service years and numbers seeking citizenship. It does not order their discharge or revoke citizenship. The retained2024§504(b) already distinguishes US nationals, lawful permanent residents, Compact categories and a conditional critical-skill enlistment authority. Retained§532 separately requires citizenship and other qualifications and permits only its specified citizenship waiver for lawful permanent residents or specified US nationals, below major/lieutenant commander, when national security requires. The new text is not a general repeal of those qualifications or a statement that every foreign-born person is ineligible. Its printed §4872(f) references and the same package's §1803 replacement of that section require the cross-reference qualification below; no unambiguous individual eligibility determination is asserted.

Section521 would add a prohibition on instruction at or attendance at a service academy under10US347 by a foreign national of a covered nation, using its printed §4872 definition reference. It is narrower than the rejected all-foreign-country replacement. The retained2024§347 otherwise authorizes selected foreign attendance, up to80 at each academy, plus separately bounded exchanges and short cultural activities. Its reimbursement rule includes a Secretary of Defense whole-or-part waiver; graduation does not itself confer entitlement to a US military appointment. Floor debate references to60 students or invariably full reimbursement are attributed statements, not substitutes for that dated statute. This candidate does not infer that the passage vote supported or opposed a particular foreign student, admission or commission.

Section529 requires the Secretary of Defense to establish by January1,2028 a foreign-student SeniorROTC participation program using existing10US2103(b), with a September30,2027 strategy, reporting and a December31,2032 termination. Existing2103(b) permits foreign enrollment when the relevant military Secretary approves under criteria approved by the Secretary of State. Section529 denies use of its authority for participating foreign students' tuition or room and board; it does not issue visas, guarantee selection or create a commission entitlement. Separate§605 removes the first-year-course condition from10US2103a(a), not from2103(a). The dated2103a(b) citizenship, enlistment and loyalty requirements are not deleted by that operand. Its contracting-bonus changes do not waive all military or immigration eligibility conditions.

Section1705 changes only the date in48US1806(b)(1)(B), before December31,2029 to before December31,2035. The retained2024 provision concerns otherwise-qualified H-2B workers, up to three years notwithstanding the temporary-service requirement, for specified military-realignment-related contractor work OR specified healthcare work at joint-serving facilities on Guam or the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. The healthcare branch retains applicable education, training and licensing conditions and excludes medical-school graduates coming to practice medicine. The location limitation and otherwise-qualified language remain. The retained law's separate transition endpoint and the §1806(b)(1)(A) transition linkage are not changed by the printed1705 operand; their interaction and any intervening law remain application questions. This is not a blanket extension of every CNMI transition/CW-1 rule, a waiver of all admission or labor requirements, or guaranteed admission through2035. EnactedDecember2025§1703 is a different, already enacted Wake Island authority with its own otherwise-qualified seeking, cap, cancellation, transfer and time-window conditions; it is not silently restated as the July1705 amendment.

Adopted Part A34 appears as §3118. It prohibits obligation or expenditure of funds authorized by this Act or otherwise available for FY2027 for DOE for a defined National Laboratory that authorizes a covered visitor's admission to a nonpublic area. A covered visitor is a foreign national from a country of concern under enactedPL119-60§8512 who is NOT a DOE employee or the laboratory's management-and-operations contractor employee AND has requested access to the laboratory's premises, information or technology; lawful permanent residents are excluded. The incorporated8512 definition is the People's Republic of China, including Hong Kong and Macau. It is not the four-country §4872 list, every foreign scientist or birthplace/ethnicity. The laboratory term retains its42US15801 statutory definition. Broader country lists or direct visitor-ban shorthand in debate do not replace this funding prohibition and its conjunctive predicates.

Section1803 prints an entire replacement of10US4872. Its covered-nation definition is in proposed(m)(5) and lists North Korea, China, Russia and Iran. Proposed(m)(13) United States person includes a US citizen, a lawful permanent resident, OR a domestically organized entity whose ultimate beneficial ownership AND control are with those persons; it is not citizenship alone. The replacement has distinct sourcing restrictions and exceptions. Proposed4872(g) gives the Secretary of Defense one conditional authority to waive(d) or(e), in whole or part, for a procurement, covered item, Tier1 or Tier2 material or supply-chain stage, including a combination or class. The waiver must be written and identify with specificity the covered materials/circumstances AND its period AND factual basis; determine insufficient Tier1 production by domestically owned entities or insufficient Tier2 production outside covered nations, in quantity, quality or form to meet timely defense needs on reasonable terms; determine that absence of the waiver would significantly adversely affect NATIONAL SECURITY OR defense production OR readiness OR sustainment OR timely contract performance; AND provide a transition plan. The adverse-effect determination may be based on or informed by a4863(k) national-security waiver, but that does not replace the other(g)(1) prerequisites. The transition plan includes quantifiable mitigation milestones/timelines, a requirement that the contractor enter binding supplier agreements before expiry that will result in compliance and obviate a future waiver/renewal, and any contractual considerations the Secretary determines appropriate. An upstream-material waiver does not cover downstream forms unless it expressly says so. A waiver may last up to two years and may be renewed without a numerical limit only on a new written determination satisfying paragraph(1). It cannot take effect until congressional-defense-committee notice and30days, or certified urgent need and7days; notice includes specificity, period, factual basis and principal mitigation measures. Contractors must supply reasonably available supporting documentation as prescribed. These are conjunctive sourcing-waiver conditions, not separate general national-security and nonavailability waiver paths. The general180day applicability rule and special Tier2 timing remain distinct, and none establishes a personal immigration ban. Elsewhere the package still prints references to4872(f),4872(d) and older subparagraphs. The retained2024 law and selected enacted2025 amendments are dated witnesses, not permission to silently repair those references or certify the outcome of all overlapping amendments. Proposed nationality/control definitions, effective dates, constitutional and individual applications remain qualified by these printed legal questions.

For the remotely crewed offshore supply-vessel pilot in§3555, all operating functions, including navigation, engineering and monitoring, must be performed by credentialed US citizens, with the same crew complement size and certification currently required for that vessel type, size and power. Eligibility is limited to specified coastwise-qualified12112 vessels built OR repaired in US shipyards within five years, no more than6,000deadweight tons/350feet, operating remotely in the Gulf beyond12nautical miles. The Commandant's design/crew-accommodation regulation modifications or waivers remain subject to navigation and safe/secure-operation conditions; they do not waive the printed operating-personnel citizenship requirement. Retained12112 has its own documentation and build/prize/forfeiture/wreck/other-law conditions. Although3555 prints a five-year nominal pilot term,1726's notwithstanding-law earlier-of-two-years-or-own-earlier-date rule must be retained; no five-year delivery promise or universal pilot-extension/post-termination conclusion follows.

Sections3563,3564 and3566 print different maritime education, credential-cost reimbursement and training-cruise assistance mechanisms. They respectively use proposed51512,51708 and51513 and expressly condition the relevant individual assistance on US citizenship. The Secretary MAY make the described agreements/payments; academy, credential, transportation-worker credential, medical, service, reporting, funding and nonduplication conditions remain. In3563/3566, the waiver or alternative-service provisions are limited to terms in subsection(c), rather than an authority to waive the subsection(a) citizenship condition. The3564 reimbursement branch requires the specified sea service OR qualifying shoreside work and retains the$10,000-per-year and other-source/program exclusions; its printed10,0000gross-register-ton wording is not repaired. These are not universal benefits or new personal entry/employment rights.

The separately printed3687 proposed51512 concerns academy fuel and crew funding, and3688 proposed51513 concerns predominantly private sea-term scholarships and student agreements. They are not silently merged with the3563/3566 texts merely because proposed Code numbers overlap; their actors, funds, service and eligibility wording differ. Section3688 does not print the same express citizenship clause as3566, but that observation does not establish that any particular noncitizen qualifies under all credential/academy/other laws. Section3683 directs a maritime exchange program limited to US citizens and citizens of NATO members, US treaty allies and major non-NATO allies, and directs the Maritime Administrator to seek corporate/government placement partners. It does not itself issue visas or guarantee a placement.

Section3691 adds periodic, at-least-annual inspection of defined offshore facilities to verify a valid43US1356(c) exemption, and confirmation that crew ALREADY REQUIRED to hold a TWIC under70105 have one. The dated1356(a)(3) regulation concerns US citizens OR lawful permanent residents and retains(c)'s contractual/registry, worker-availability, national-interest and foreign-ownership/control/reciprocity exceptions. Dated70105 has defined access/credential categories, security and immigration checks, waiver/appeal and privacy rules; it is not a universal citizens-only crew rule. The July inspection language does not itself repeal those exceptions or impose a TWIC on every person aboard every vessel.

Section3569's proposed vessel-preference subchapter concerns defined inbound containerized and roll-on/roll-off vehicle cargo within designated trade lanes, with entity/group participation targets, mariner/fleet/capacity findings and specified phase adjustments. It expressly disclaims a uniform nationwide cargo quota. Its qualification condition distinguishes a vessel owned, chartered, managed or operated by or for an entity subject to foreign ownership, control or influence from an entity determined not to be so subject; the former needs an approved M-SSA. The separate country-of-concern prohibition combines a citizen's country status with a direct or indirect controlling interest OR other disqualifying influence in the owner/charterer/manager/operator. Nationality alone is not the complete printed predicate.

For the M-SSA framework, the Secretary of Transportation must establish regulations in consultation with Defense and Homeland Security, while the Maritime Administrator MAY approve an agreement only with the three printed certification/compliance/consultation conditions. The covered entity must maintain the specified US-citizen executive, citizen governance and operational-control arrangements, citizen-only security committee, citizen compliance officers and sensitive-information firewalls. These are specified operational/governance roles, not a rule that every foreign investor or employee is prohibited. The agreement's entity/vessel scope, change notice/approval, audit, breach/remedy and information-security conditions remain. Its limited deeming concerns an approved entity being United States-controlled, with the separate capital-origin condition; it does not naturalize anyone or confer coastwise privileges. Existing documentation, safety, security, labor and other national-security reviews are not waived. Printed references to regulations under55353(j), the55352 content/deeming cross-references, duplicate definition number6, overlapping2042 threshold, and PhaseI's minimum four-year pilot-period language alongside1726 remain application questions, without silently selecting a repaired provision or imposing a two-year end on the whole cargo regime.

The country definitions are not interchangeable. Section3569 imports countries identified under15US4651(7). That dated definition enumerates category(A), a covered nation under its printed4872(d) reference, and category(B), any country the Commerce Secretary determines, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, Secretary of State and Director of National Intelligence, engages in conduct detrimental to US national security or foreign policy. Section3604 separately enumerates a covered-nation category(A) under its own printed4872(d) reference and category(B), any country the Maritime Administrator so determines in consultation with the named Defense/State/Intelligence officials AND the Chair of the Federal Maritime Commission. The literal connecting and is retained as an enumeration of the two described country categories, not a requirement that a country satisfy both category descriptions. The Commerce and Maritime actors/consultations and printed outdated or overlapping references remain distinct and qualified. Neither definition is silently replaced with3118's China/HongKong/Macau definition or a universal fixed-country list. Section3569's incorporated-reference and application questions are not resolved by restating the enumeration.

Section3604's foreign-entity definition separately describes foreign government/party, natural-person and foreign-organization branches and broader owned/controlled/directed, agent/employee, substantial-equity, managerial and country-citizenship/residence inclusion branches. The natural-person branch excludes lawful permanent residents, US citizens and other protected individuals under8US1324b(a)(3). The dated protected-individual definition includes US nationals and specified temporary residents, refugees and asylees with its printed qualifications. The independent express LPR exclusion is not removed merely by a qualification in the other-protected-person branch. Conversely, that one natural-person branch does not erase the other agency/control/inclusion limbs. No individual is classified by birthplace or ethnicity. This title's distinct foreign-entity-of-concern alternatives include particular designations, lists, jurisdiction/control, alleged activity with obtained convictions, carrier findings and a specified official determination; it does not label every foreign national a terrorist, sanctioned person or immigration offender.

Sections1041–1043 change the named2019 Guantanamo funding restrictions' December31,2026 endpoints to December31,2027;1044 changes the named2018 station-control restriction's fiscal-year endpoint2026 to2027. The selected original1033 restriction concerns its named/qualified detainee population and transfer/release assistance to or within the United States, territories or possessions, not all migrants. Original1034 includes its Guantanamo-facility modification exception and the incorporated2015 defined population; original1035 names Libya, Somalia, Syria and Yemen. The station provision concerns closing/abandoning, relinquishing control to Cuba or the specified constructive treaty change. The selected enacted2025 extensions supply the2026 operands. These dated original and intervening witnesses do not establish exhaustive current law or permit importing an unrestricted detention/transfer rule. Section1045 separately inserts an exclusion for a US citizen into FY2012§1021(b)'s covered-person definition under the named AUMF framework. The retained1021/1022 text has specific hostile-conduct/person predicates and savings/other-law rules. Excluding citizens from that definition is not a new authority to detain every noncitizen or a resolution of constitutional or individual detention questions.

Section1081(jj) strikes FY2022NDAA§1324. The complete original1324 requires recurring notices of OAW or successor-operation transportation, housing, medical and other sustainment costs for Afghan special-immigrant-visa applicants and other Afghans at risk, and whether those funds were reimbursable. Repealing that notification is not itself repeal of all OAW spending, assistance or admission authorities. The bill's label and the baseline's civic-aid wording remain separate literal texts. Section1082 extends the named quarterly southwest-border support briefing endpoint from2026 to2027, retaining the original briefing's planning, personnel-risk, Mexico-cooperation, support, readiness and recommendation subjects; it does not direct a new deployment or confer an admission or arrest power.

The actual border common-picture provision is1089R, which requires a Secretary of Defense plan within180days and later communication to interagency partners the Secretary considers appropriate. Its architecture/data sources, sharing procedures and authorities, cybersecurity/data protection, coordination with named domestic and authorized international partners, phased schedule, resources, training and effectiveness metrics are plan requirements, not proof of deployed capability or unrestricted surveillance. Separate1089 concerns autonomous-warfare doctrine and is not substituted for1089R. Section1099A directs a named operation for specified southwest-border support and the related budget/request/oversight reporting, and expressly disclaims authorization of military force. Its definition includes specified planning/logistics/intelligence/aviation/engineering support but expressly excludes support provided to a civilian law-enforcement agency; that printed tension is retained. Section1065 calls for a revised instrument named Department of Defense Instruction3025.18 requiring reassessment of immediate-response necessity no later than one week after the request, plus notification of issuance by the printed deadline. It does not authorize limitless response. The Instruction label in1065 and Directive label in1099A, incorporated versions and any resulting legal application are not silently repaired or certified.
